related.prompt: Is momentum canonically conjugate to position?

chain: The conjugate variable of position is energy. (edit)
conjugate_to is functional, so position has one conjugate variable, and it is energy.
So momentum is no longer the conjugate variable of position: no.

Being conjugate to is symmetric, and conjugate_to is functional (position has one conjugate variable), so position's is energy and momentum no longer is.
So position is not canonically conjugate to momentum: no.

Position is canonically conjugate to mom.why: Position and momentum are the standard example of a canonical pair, named together wherever the commutation relation or the uncertainty principle is introduced, so the symmetric reading (position conjugate to momentum) is itself a common sentence, not an inference people make.

notes: Dev-split ABox revision (14 queries, all determinate, no worlds); the edit carries symmetry. Physics has few symmetric relations between named things whose partner is unique: antiparticle_of is taken by records/physics (replace-0018 and delete-0018 use the positron, the electron and the proton as instances), isotope_of, attracts and in_thermal_equilibrium_with are many-valued, and mirror nuclei are too obscure for the audit models. The conjugate pairs of quantum mechanics are well known, symmetric and, for the pairs used here (position and momentum, energy and time), have one partner each, so conjugate_to (staging/physics.RELATIONS.md) is tagged symmetric and functional. Caveat recorded: Wikipedia's Conjugate variables article also lists time with frequency (proportional to energy) and position with wavenumber (proportional to momentum); those are the same pairs up to a constant, and no query uses them. Related near asks the conjugate of energy: by symmetry it is position, and by functionality time drops out. Related far reaches position by its operator symbol x̂ (binding: "x̂ is the position operator" is a separate fact, checked before editing) and asks its conjugate; the stored form is the commutation relation [x̂, p̂] = iħ and "the momentum conjugate to x". It replaced, in review, a Heisenberg question ("the more precisely position is known, the less precisely which quantity?"): the uncertainty relation is part of what conjugate_to means in the catalogue, so that question was the edit in other words (1 hop), and "inheritance" did not fit it. Residual risk: a model may read x̂ as a mere abbreviation of "position", making the binding close to a paraphrase; the symbol is still a separate name the model has to connect, and a model that keeps [x̂, p̂] = iħ as a stored formula answers momentum, which is the stored answer not yet overturned that related far measures. Derived: three compositions that look up a stored fact about energy (its SI unit, that it is a scalar, its operator). Near unrelated asks the SI unit of momentum, which the edit does not touch and whose reference differs from the new answer. Counts are exact-phrase Dolma counts unless marked approximate.
